_pricing_meta.notes: gpt-5.6 family added 2026-07-30. gpt-5.6-sol is the flagship (gpt-5.6 is its alias); -terra and -luna are the mid and light tiers. DIVERGENCE, needs a human: OpenRouter's public price sheet - fetched live in the same pass and used verbatim for the openrouter provider entry - agrees exactly on gpt-5.6-sol ($5/$30 per 1M) and on gpt-5-nano ($0.05/$0.40), but quotes gpt-5.6-terra at $1/$6 and gpt-5.6-luna at $0.10/$0.60, i.e. one tier lower than the vendor rates recorded here. Those two are flagged needs_verification; the direct-API rates are kept because overestimating cost is the safe direction for a budget gate.

claude-sonnet-5 is on introductory pricing ($2/$10 per 1M) which rises to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01, see the `scheduled` block on that entry. cache_write / cache_read are the prompt-cache rates in $/1k, copied from the published per-model table at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing (5m cache write = 1.25x base input, 1h cache write = 2x, cache read = 0.1x). cache_write is the 5-MINUTE write rate: FERAL never sends cache_control.ttl, so every cache write it can incur is the 5m kind. cost/pricing.py reads input/output/cache_write/cache_read and ignores every other key; a model with no cache_* rate has its cache tokens left unbilled rather than billed at a guessed rate.

anthropic._models_note: Since the 4.6 generation Anthropic model ids use a DATELESS format that is itself a pinned snapshot — appending a date suffix 404s. claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 predates that change and keeps its date; claude-haiku-4-5 is its alias.
anthropic._capabilities_note: sampling_params records whether temperature / top_p / top_k are accepted. They were REMOVED in Claude 4.7 (HTTP 400), so it tracks thinking.adaptive from 4.7 onward - but NOT for Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6, which are adaptive-capable and still accept sampling params. Those two carry an explicit true.

_pricing_meta.notes: gemini-3.1-pro-preview is TIERED on prompt length: $2/$12 per 1M at or below 200K input tokens, $4/$18 above it. The flat input/output fields carry the <=200K tier (the common case); the `tiers` list carries both so a length-aware estimator can pick the right one. There is no stable `gemini-3.1-pro` id — the -preview suffix is part of the model id.
